definitions.explanation: The state of not dying or being unable to die. Used in mythology, fantasy, religion, and figurative expressions about things that endure.

examples.japanese: {不死|ふし}の{力|ちから}を{手|て}に{入|い}れた。
examples.english: He obtained the power of immortality.

examples.japanese: {不死|ふし}の{存在|そんざい}は{神話|しんわ}によく{登場|とうじょう}する。
examples.english: Immortal beings appear frequently in mythology.

examples.japanese: {古代|こだい}の{皇帝|こうてい}は{不死|ふし}の{薬|くすり}を{求|もと}めて{世界中|せかいじゅう}に{使者|ししゃ}を{送|おく}ったと{言|い}われている。
examples.english: It is said that ancient emperors sent envoys around the world in search of an elixir of immortality.

notes:
Literally "not" ({不|ふ}) + "death" ({死|し}). Used in mythology, fantasy fiction, and games.

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
・{不死|ふし}の{体|からだ} (immortal body)
・{不死|ふし}の{存在|そんざい} (immortal being)
・{不死|ふし}の{薬|くすり} (elixir of immortality)
・{不死身|ふじみ} (invulnerability — a related but distinct word)

RELATED WORDS:
・{不老不死|ふろうふし}: eternal youth and immortality (a four-character compound)
・{不死身|ふじみ}: invulnerable, indestructible (used more casually; can describe someone tough)
・{永遠|えいえん}の{命|いのち}: eternal life

cross_references.notes: 節 (ふし) means joint, knot, or melody — same reading, different meaning
